bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷十六 唐廢帝家人傳第四:
title.en: Volume 16: Family of the Tang Deposed Emperor
title.raw: 卷十六 唐廢帝家人傳第四: Volume 16: Family of the Tang Deposed Emperor

translations.literal: Empress Liu of the Deposed Emperor
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu, wife of the deposed Later Tang emperor.

translations.literal: The Two Sons of the Deposed Emperor

sentences.zh: 廢帝二子，曰重吉、重美，一女為尼，號幼澄，皆不知其所生。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor's two sons were named Chongji and Chongmei; one daughter became a Buddhist nun, styled Youcheng; none of them is known by whom they were born.
translations.idiomatic: His sons bore the names Chongji and Chongmei; a daughter took vows as a nun under the sobriquet Youcheng. History does not record who bore any of them.

translations.literal: The way of the "Family" cannot fail to be set right.
translations.idiomatic: The norms that govern household and kin must be upheld.

sentences.zh: 夫禮者，所以別嫌而明微也。

translations.literal: Now ritual is that whereby one separates what is suspect and makes clear what is subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual exists precisely to dispel doubt and bring fine distinctions to light.

sentences.zh: 甚矣，五代之際，君君臣臣父父子子之道乖，而宗廟、朝廷，人鬼皆失其序，斯可謂亂世者歟！

translations.literal: Extreme! At the time of the Five Dynasties, the way of lord and lord, minister and minister, father and father, son and son went awry; at the ancestral temple and at court, both the living and the dead lost their proper order—this may indeed be called an age of chaos!
translations.idiomatic: How far things had fallen! In the Five Dynasties the reciprocal duties of ruler and ruled, father and child, collapsed together; temple and palace alike were scenes where neither men nor shades kept their station—truly an era of disorder!

translations.literal: From antiquity onward there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing like it appears in the earlier record.

sentences.zh: 唐一號而三姓，周一號而二姓。

translations.literal: Tang bore one reign title but three surnames; Zhou bore one reign title but two surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The house called Tang ruled under a single dynastic name yet passed through three clans; the house called Zhou did the same with two.

sentences.zh: 唐太祖、莊宗為一家，明宗、湣帝為一家，廢帝為一家；

translations.literal: Tang Taizu and Zhuangzong were one family; Mingzong and the Min Emperor were one family; the Deposed Emperor was one family;
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang thus falls into three bloodlines: Taizu and Zhuangzong; Mingzong and the short-reigned Min emperor; and the deposed emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 周太祖為一家，世宗為一家。

translations.literal: Zhou Taizu was one family, Shizong was one family.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou likewise splits in two: the line of Taizu and that of Shizong.

sentences.zh: 別其家而同其號者，何哉？

translations.literal: They distinguish their families yet share the same dynastic name—why is that?
translations.idiomatic: Why, then, does the chronicle cleave the clans yet leave the dynastic label unchanged?

sentences.zh: 唐從其號，見其盜而有也；

translations.literal: For Tang, following its name shows that they stole it yet came to possess it;
translations.idiomatic: For Later Tang the shared name exposes naked usurpation: each claimant seized the throne from the last.

translations.literal: for Zhou, following its name means it was given to them.
translations.idiomatic: For Later Zhou the single title marks legitimate succession: the mandate was handed down within the alliance that founded the state.

sentences.zh: 而別其家者，昭穆親疏之不可亂也。

translations.literal: But distinguishing their families is because senior and junior generations, close and distant kin, cannot be confused.
translations.idiomatic: The separate "families" preserve the temple order of fathers and sons, near kin and far—lines that must not be blurred.

sentences.zh: 號可同，家不可以不別，所以別嫌而明微也。

translations.literal: The name may be the same; families cannot fail to be distinguished—this is to separate suspicion and clarify the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic names may repeat; agnatic lines may not. That, again, is the work of ritual: clearing doubt and marking fine shades.

sentences.zh: 梁博王友文之不別，何哉？

translations.literal: The Prince of Bo of Liang, You Wen—why was no family distinction drawn for him?
translations.idiomatic: Why, then, does the Later Liang record leave Bo Prince You Wen outside the neat partition of "families" that I have just defended?

sentences.zh: 著禍本也，梁太祖之禍，自友文始，存之所以戒也。

translations.literal: It is to write down the root of calamity: the calamity of Liang Taizu began with You Wen; keeping this unresolved exists in order to warn.
translations.idiomatic: Because the historian means to expose the taproot: the founder of Later Liang brought ruin on himself starting with You Wen, and the deliberate ambiguity in the record is itself the lesson for posterity.
